Name: uav_night_small_objects
Title: Does synthetic low-light augmentation of daytime UAV imagery transfer to real night scenes for small objects?
Short Hypothesis: Fine-tuning a small detector on daytime VisDrone images with physics-inspired synthetic low-light degradation raises small-object AP on real night VisDrone images, while test-time enhancement (gamma, CLAHE) helps small objects less than medium ones because it amplifies noise.
Related Work: VisDrone2019-DET (Zhu et al., TPAMI 2021) is a dense small-object UAV benchmark without illumination labels. MAET (Cui et al., ICCV 2021) synthesizes low-light training data with an unprocess/noise/ISP pipeline and evaluates COCO to ExDark, not UAV or object size. Lv et al. (IJCV 2021) simulate low light with noise. Zero-DCE++ (Li et al., TPAMI 2021) enhances without paired data. IA-YOLO (AAAI 2022), FeatEnHancer (ICCV 2023) and YOLA (NeurIPS 2024) learn illumination handling end to end; YOLA reports that several enhancers reduce detection AP on ExDark and notes that enhancement can impair small faces. PFNN (Frontiers in AI 2025) compared enhancers on an unpublished VisDrone night subset without size bins. Bridge (CVPR 2026) sets a day-to-dark protocol on DroneVehicle without augmentation baselines or size analysis. SAHI (ICIP 2022) and P2 heads improve VisDrone small objects but do not address illumination. To our knowledge no study measures synthetic-to-real low-light transfer by object size on UAV imagery; this is not a verified novelty claim.
Abstract: DATA: download VisDrone2019-DET train, val and test-dev zips from https://github.com/ultralytics/assets/releases/download/v0.0.0/ (VisDrone2019-DET-train.zip, VisDrone2019-DET-val.zip, VisDrone2019-DET-test-dev.zip) on the remote machine only, caching under /content/cache/visdrone and reusing the cache when present (check for a completion marker file, never re-download). Convert annotations to YOLO format like the Ultralytics VisDrone.yaml: drop class 0 (ignored regions) and class 11 (others), keep the 10 classes, clip boxes. PRE-REGISTERED ILLUMINATION GROUPS: per-image median luma of the grayscale image resized to a 256 px long side, in [0,1]. day: median >= 0.30; night: median < 0.16; twilight: in between. Splits: day-train and day-tune come from train-split day images, split 90/10 by sequence id (the first underscore-separated filename field) with a fixed seed 0; day-test is val-split day images; night-test pools night images from train, val and test-dev (training uses day images only, so no image overlap); twilight-test pools twilight images from val and test-dev. Print and save group counts per split and a montage of 24 random night-test images. Real night images must never be used for training, tuning, early stopping or model selection. DETECTOR: Ultralytics YOLOv8n fine-tuned from COCO-pretrained yolov8n.pt, imgsz 640, identical epochs, batch, optimizer, schedule and augmentation for every arm; only the training images differ. Use cache='ram' or 'disk' when memory allows, workers set to the available CPU count, verbose=False, plots=False, and write Ultralytics run directories under /content/cache/runs, not the job workspace; copy only small result files back. SYNTHETIC LOW LIGHT (arm B): for a seeded random 50% of day-train images, write a degraded copy that replaces the original, keeping the image count equal to arm A: convert sRGB to linear (gamma 2.2), multiply by exposure k ~ LogUniform(0.05, 0.3), add Poisson-Gaussian noise in linear space with shot variance a*x, a ~ LogUniform(1e-4, 1e-2) and read-noise std s ~ LogUniform(1e-3, 1e-2), clip, re-apply gamma 1/2.2, quantize to uint8 JPEG quality 95. Degraded copies depend on the training seed. The same pipeline with a fixed seed 12345 creates synthetic-dark versions of day-tune and day-test. TEST-TIME ENHANCEMENT: apply to night-test and twilight-test images before inference for arms A and B: none; gamma correction with exponent chosen per image to map its median luma to 0.35 (clip the exponent to [0.3, 1]); CLAHE on the LAB L channel (clipLimit 2.0, tile 8x8). EVALUATION: run inference at imgsz 640, conf 0.001, max_det 1000, map predictions to original resolution, and evaluate with pycocotools COCOeval against ground truth converted to COCO JSON at original resolution. Report AP, AP50 and AP by area bin at original resolution: tiny (<16^2), small (16^2 to 32^2), small_all (<32^2, the primary endpoint), medium (32^2 to 96^2) and large, per set: day-tune, synthetic-dark-tune, day-test, synthetic-dark-test, night-test, twilight-test. Selection metric for choosing configurations: mean of AP on day-tune and synthetic-dark-tune only. Report real night metrics labelled report_only. COMPUTE: target at most 40 minutes wall clock per script including a first-time download and preparation on a fresh VM; the hard limit is 50 minutes. Measure seconds per epoch and choose epochs to fit; prefer the L4 tier when training two arms. Read the training seed from os.environ.get('AUTORESEARCH_SEED', '0') and keep data splits and synthetic test degradations fixed across seeds. Print the GPU name, torch and ultralytics versions (as str), epoch time and total runtime. Save every metric, count, setting, seed and version in experiment_data.npy (keep it under 5 MB; store at most 8 small uint8 example images) and never fabricate or estimate a metric that was not computed. Plotting and metric parsing run locally without torch or a GPU: use only numpy, matplotlib and the standard library. Do not call these numbers comparable to published VisDrone results, which use 300 or more epochs.
Experiments: Stage 1: implement the data pipeline, illumination grouping, COCO evaluation and both training arms with a short schedule; verify counts, the night montage and finite metrics.
Stage 2: tune only the shared training schedule (epochs, learning rate, batch) for the baseline within the time limit using the selection metric; the same settings are then used for every arm.

Stage 3: main comparison of arm A (unchanged day images) and arm B (50% synthetic low-light) with test-time none/gamma/CLAHE, three seeds, paired per-seed differences in small_all AP on night-test, and the day-test guard.

Stage 4 ablations of arm B: darkening without noise, noise level range, replacement fraction 0.25 and 0.75, and an optional warm colour cast typical of sodium street lights; report which component carries any real-night gain.
Report negative and null results; state effect sizes against seed variability rather than significance.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Night is defined by a luminance threshold, not by capture metadata; misassigned dusk or shaded daytime images can bias night-test.
Night-test scenes share locations with daytime training scenes, and VisDrone night images are few and concentrated in a few sequences.
Short fine-tuning schedules at 640 px underfit tiny objects, so absolute AP is low and not comparable to published results.
Ignored regions are dropped, so detections inside them count as false positives equally in every arm.
Three training seeds do not capture dataset variability; conclusions are limited to VisDrone and YOLOv8n.
Synthetic degradation gains alone do not support H1; only real night-test results do.
